title: Cortex Connector Protocol
description: Every frame exchanged over the Cortex connector WebSocket (ws://127.0.0.1:5080/connector). One WebSocket TEXT message carries exactly one frame, UTF-8 encoded. Unknown fields are ignored and field names are matched case-insensitively, so a connector must tolerate additive protocol changes. See docs/connector-plugin-system.md for semantics; this schema is the shape only.

connectorId.description: Connector key or instance id. Normalised to lowercase by the Bridge.

entityId.description: messageId, conversationId or sender.id. REJECTED (not truncated) when longer than the maximum. Length is counted in UTF-16 code units.

isoTimestamp.description: ISO-8601 timestamp. Round-trip cursors verbatim rather than reformatting them.

capabilities.description: Declared in hello. Each capability is an opt-in; the Bridge never enables one the connector did not ask for, and an operator can disable any of them globally.

streaming.description: Receive typing and stream frames during generation.

media.description: Send and receive content.attachments. Without it, inbound attachments are refused with media_not_supported and outbound frames omit the field entirely.

maxMessageLength.description: Maximum inbound text length the connector accepts, in UTF-16 code units. Clamped by the Bridge to [1, 100000].

attachment.description: A media attachment. The SAME shape is used inbound and outbound. Exactly one of data or handle carries the bytes. There is deliberately no url field: the Bridge never dereferences a connector-supplied location, and a frame containing url is rejected with invalid_payload rather than having the field ignored.

mimeType.description: Declared type. VERIFIED against the content's magic bytes - mislabelled content is rejected with attachment_type_not_allowed.

fileName.description: Display name. Sanitised (path separators, control and Unicode-format characters removed) and truncated to 256 UTF-16 code units.

caption.description: Alt text. Truncated to 1024 UTF-16 code units.

data.description: Base64-encoded bytes, for attachments small enough to fit the frame. Mutually exclusive with handle.

handle.description: Opaque Bridge-issued id for attachments transferred out of band. Single-use, expiring, and scoped to the issuing channel. Mutually exclusive with data.

sizeBytes.description: Declared size. A HINT ONLY - the Bridge verifies the actual decoded length and never trusts this value.

content.description: Message content. Must carry text, attachments, or both.

text.description: Message text. Length counted in UTF-16 code units against maxMessageLength.

attachments.description: Requires capabilities.media. More than maxAttachmentsPerMessage (default 4) is refused with too_many_attachments.

helloFrame.description: Connector -> Bridge. MUST be the first frame, within 10 seconds of connecting.

displayName.description: Shown in the Web UI. UNTRUSTED there - it is escaped on render. Truncated to 256 UTF-16 code units.

version.description: The CONNECTOR's own version, not the protocol version. Informational: the Bridge stores it for display and does not act on it. There is no protocol version negotiation.

token.description: The durable token from a previous paired frame. Omit on first connect to start the pairing flow.

sinceCursor.description: Replay from this point. Absent OR unparseable means NO replay - unparseable fails closed rather than replaying everything.

inboundFrame.description: Connector -> Bridge. A user message. Rate-limited to maxMessagesPerMinute (default 120).

conversationId.description: Opaque thread key chosen by the connector. Defaults to the channel id.

messageId.description: Auto-generated when absent. NOT deduplicated - a repeated id is treated as a new message.

displayName.description: TRUNCATED at 256 UTF-16 code units rather than rejected.

abortFrame.description: Connector -> Bridge. Cancels an in-flight generation. Only conversations this session has previously sent an inbound for may be aborted; at most 256 are tracked.

pongFrame.description: Connector -> Bridge. Reply to ping. The session closes if no frame of any kind arrives within 90 seconds.

pairingRequiredFrame.description: Bridge -> Connector. Display the code and wait; there is no timeout on the connector side.

code.description: Always 8 characters shaped XXXX-XXX, from an alphabet excluding 0, 1, I and O. The human compares it with the Web UI.

pairedFrame.description: Bridge -> Connector. Pairing approved. Persist the token; a ready frame follows.

token.description: Durable credential. Present it in hello.token, and as an Authorization: Bearer value on the attachment endpoints. Store it as securely as the platform allows.

pairingDeniedFrame.description: Bridge -> Connector. FATAL - the socket closes. Do not reconnect immediately.

reason.description: Known values: denied, pairing_expired, pairing_rate_limited, connector_disabled, shutting_down. Treat an unknown reason as a plain denial.

readyFrame.description: Bridge -> Connector. Steady state. Always arrives BEFORE any replay frames.

replayCount.description: How many outbound frames of replay to expect before live traffic.

typingFrame.description: Bridge -> Connector. Only sent when capabilities.streaming is true.

streamFrame.description: Bridge -> Connector. A text delta. Only sent when capabilities.streaming is true. Concatenate deltas in arrival order; the outbound frame carries the final text.

outboundFrame.description: Bridge -> Connector. The final agent response, or a replayed message. ALWAYS persist cursor and send it back as hello.sinceCursor.

conversationId.description: On REPLAYED frames this is the channel id, not the original conversation id.

content.description: attachments is present only when capabilities.media was declared. An attachment arrives EITHER inline (data) OR as a handle - implement both, since the Bridge inlines what fits the frame and spills anything larger.

isThinking.description: True for pre-tool narration rather than the final answer.

errorFrame.description: Bridge -> Connector. Fatality depends on the code AND, for invalid_payload, on whether the session was established. See the error table in docs/connector-plugin-system.md.

code.description: Always fatal: malformed_frame, unknown_frame_type, protocol_violation, frame_too_large, connector_limit_reached, duplicate_connector, connectors_disabled. Never fatal: message_too_long, rate_limited, media_not_supported, too_many_attachments, attachment_too_large, attachment_type_not_allowed, attachment_not_found. Conditional: invalid_payload is FATAL before ready, recoverable after. Defined but never sent: not_paired. Treat an UNKNOWN code as non-fatal and back off.

pingFrame.description: Bridge -> Connector. Sent every 30 seconds. Reply with pong.
